ZstdSharp.Port 0.8.5 (MIT), the pure managed Zstandard port: https://github.com/oleg-st/ZstdSharp
Only lib\net462\ZstdSharp.dll is vendored. The KSP client loads it late-bound (LmpCommon\PersistentSync\ZstdBackend.cs) and
uses it to decompress AND compress. KSP's Managed folder has no netstandard.dll, so the net462 build is used.

Helper DLL set the client ships (all net461/net462-style builds, none needs netstandard.dll; KSP's Mono binds by name and
ignores versions, so what matters is which file KSP loads, not the version ZstdSharp was built against):

  System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe  6.0.0   (assembly 6.0.0.0, lib\net461)  was 4.5.3 (4.0.4.1)   <-- the fix
  System.Memory                           4.5.4   (4.0.1.1)   unchanged  (ZstdSharp asks for 4.0.1.2, Mono does not care)
  System.Buffers                          4.5.1   (4.0.3.0)   unchanged
  System.Numerics.Vectors                 4.5.0   (4.1.4.0)   unchanged
  System.Threading.Tasks.Extensions       4.5.4   (4.2.0.1)   unchanged, lives in this folder (see below)

Why Unsafe 6.0.0: ZstdSharp's compressor calls Unsafe.SkipInit<T>(ref T), added in System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe 5.0.
With Unsafe 4.5.3 decompression worked but every compress call died with
"MissingMethodException: Method not found: 'Void System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe.SkipInit(!!0 ByRef)'" (first hit in
ZSTD_buildSequencesStatistics), so the client fell back to QuickLZ. Unsafe 6.0.0 is exactly the version ZstdSharp references
(6.0.0.0), has a net461 build (mscorlib-only, no netstandard.dll) and is a strict superset of 4.5.x, so the Lidgren/CachedQuickLz
code that was compiled against 4.0.4.1 keeps working. Nothing else had to change: the System.Memory/System.Buffers/Vectors
members ZstdSharp touches exist in the older builds. Verified offline with a harness that loads the packed client's DLLs in a
.NET Framework process and maps every requested version of these assemblies to the file in the folder, as Mono does: levels 1,
3, 9 and 15, payloads of 0 B, 1 KB and 1 MB, compress and decompress, plus MessageCodec end to end.

Where the 6.0.0 DLL comes from: LmpClient.csproj (PackageReference + Reference/HintPath under
External\Nuget\System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe.6.0.0\lib\net461), synced from the NuGet cache by
Scripts\BootstrapLocalBuild.ps1. It is NOT vendored in this folder: the build output (LmpClient\bin, then Build\<cfg>\Client\Plugins)
carries it. The 4.5.3 package stays in the bootstrap map because Lidgren and the master servers still compile against it.

Other mods: KSP's AssemblyLoader keeps ONE copy per assembly name, the highest version, no matter which mod shipped it. Mods that
ship an older Unsafe (KSPBurst ships 4.0.5.0, file 4.700.20.12001) lose to our 6.0.0.0, which is API-compatible with theirs. If a mod
ships something even newer it wins; any copy of 5.0 or newer still compresses. If some mod's copy that is older than 5.0 ever wins,
ZstdBackend's self test fails, the client logs "compresses with zstd: False" and sends QuickLZ (it still decodes zstd).

System.Threading.Tasks.Extensions.dll (4.5.4, MIT, lib\net461 build, copied from External\Nuget) sits next to ZstdSharp.dll because
ZstdSharp's async stream types reference it and KSP has no copy: without it KSP's add-on checker pops up "ZstdSharp failed
to load: missing System.Threading.Tasks.Extensions" on every launch. The net461 build only references mscorlib and Unsafe, which the
client ships; the netstandard2.0 build would need netstandard.dll, which KSP lacks.
